name: Chip
summary: A 28 px pill with a short text label: a property (static), a stage (static, or pressable to advance), or a filter (toggle with aria-pressed). The variant decides whether it is a <span> or a <button>. Not for removable items (there are none in the product) and not for status with a semantic colour — Chip has no tone.

pattern.name: Toggle button (filter) via WAI-ARIA APG Button with aria-pressed; plain button (cycling stage); no pattern for the static forms

children.intent: The visible label and the accessible name. Short — one or two words: 'Orbit', 'Interview', 'Hybrid'. A chip always has visible text; there is no icon-only chip.

variant.intent: property = static fact (company, location) → <span>. stage = pipeline stage → <span>, or <button> when onPress is given (cycling). filter = toggle → <button aria-pressed>. The variant is the only thing that decides the element.

emphasis.intent: Visual weight without semantic meaning. quiet = border + text-subtle (every stage by default). tint = accent-subtle bg + accent text (the handoff's Interview). strong = accent bg + on-accent (Offer). One strong per screen — it is the accent. The stage → emphasis mapping lives in the StageChip pattern, not here.

isSelected.intent: filter only. Controlled pressed state → aria-pressed. Selected is never colour-only: inverse colours AND a heavier weight.

onChange.intent: filter only. Fires with the new boolean. Giving onChange to a non-filter chip is a type error.

onPress.intent: stage only. Turns the chip into a <button>; the pattern advances the stage, swaps the label and shows the Undo toast. Shift+→ / Shift+← are the pattern's keys, not the chip's.

aria-label.intent: Only for a cycling stage, to say what pressing does: 'Stage: Screen. Press to advance'. Never on a static chip — the label is the name.

isDisabled.intent: Interactive variants only. A disabled filter stays visible so the user sees the option exists.

iconStart.intent: Decorative, aria-hidden — the tick / dash on a priority chip. The meaning (met / not met) must also be in text: pass it as a visually-hidden suffix in children, never rely on the glyph.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to / from an interactive chip (filter, or stage with onPress). Static chips are never tab stops.
filter: toggles aria-pressed. stage with onPress: presses (the pattern advances the stage).
Not the chip's. The StageChip pattern binds them on the row to advance / revert.

a11y.name: The label text. A cycling stage may override with aria-label to describe the action ('Stage: Screen. Press to advance').
a11y.announcements: filter → aria-pressed="true" / "false" (React Aria ToggleButton). Cycling stage → the label text changes; the stage change itself is announced by the pattern's Undo toast (role="status"), so the chip adds no live region of its own. Static chips have no role and announce nothing.
a11y.targetSize: 28 × 28 px (size.target.sm): above the 24 px AA floor (2.5.8), below the 44 px touch guidance. Relies on the spacing exception — the pattern keeps ≥ 8 px (space.200) between chips so adjacent targets do not overlap. Static chips are not targets.

rules: The variant decides the element. property and stage render a <span> with no role; filter renders a <button aria-pressed>; stage renders a <button> only when onPress is given. Interactivity never comes from onClick on a span.
Selected (filter) is never colour-only: inverse background + inverse text + weight-strong + aria-pressed. Remove any one of the four and a group of users loses the state.
A filter chip's border is color.border.strong (3:1 against the surface — it is a control, 1.4.11). Static chips use color.border.default, which is decorative and exempt.

No tone. The product rule is one accent per screen; emphasis (quiet / tint / strong) is the only colour axis, and strong is that single accent. Status colours belong to text and rings in the patterns, not to chips.

A tick / dash glyph on a priority chip is decorative. The state is in text: children = 'Hybrid' + a visually-hidden ', met' — so the name reads 'Hybrid, met' and the glyph can be dropped without loss.
The cycling stage chip announces by changing its own label; the stage change is confirmed by the pattern's toast (role=status). Do not add aria-live to the chip — two announcements for one change.
28 px is a deliberate compact target: patterns must keep ≥ 8 px between chips (2.5.8 spacing exception). Do not shrink the gap to fit a row; wrap instead.
Focus ring is outline + outline-offset on the pill, never box-shadow alone; in forced-colors mode the pill keeps a ButtonText border and selected uses Highlight / HighlightText.

properties.State: browser states (default/hover/focus/active) + isSelected + isDisabled — interactive variants only
properties.Label: children

examples.title: Stage, cycling
examples.code: <Chip variant="stage" aria-label="Stage: Screen. Press to advance" onPress={advance}>Screen</Chip>
